..
Issued at 1031 PM CDT Sun Sep 6 2026

Tonight and Monday...

Water vapor imagery and objective analysis late this evening depicts 
a high amplitude mid-level ridge over the central CONUS, with a 
cutoff low moving into the Pacific Northwest. A shortwave trough 
pushing around the ridge and into extreme eastern NE and western IA 
brought scattered thunderstorms to the area this evening. A few 
showers may linger into the overnight period as a branch of the LLJ 
noses into the area along with some low-level moisture transport. 
Otherwise the broader cluster of thunderstorms over western Iowa 
pushed an outflow boundary westward into the area this evening, 
bringing a noticeably cooler air mass to portions of the area. 
Overnight lows are expected to dip into the upper 60s to low 70s.

Into the beginning of the work week, the aforementioned Pacific 
northwest low will gradually deepen and pull east along the 
US/Canada border, helping to flatten the ridge in place and push a 
cold front through the area on Tuesday. A tightening surface 
pressure gradient ahead of the approaching system and mixing into 
stronger winds aloft will bring southerly wind gusts of 25-35 mph on 
Monday. High temperatures will remain above average, peaking in the 
low to mid 90s for most. 

Another round of showers and thunderstorms is expected Monday night 
into early Tuesday as the main wave approaches. Additional support 
will come from a 45-50 kt LLJ streaming low-level moisture transport 
into the area. In response, elevated thunderstorms are expected to 
develop late Monday evening into the overnight period. A few strong 
to severe storms will be possible as MUCAPE values reach 1250-1500 
J/kg and bulk shear around 25 kts, though these values improve over 
the north side of the NE/SD line. Pockets of hail and gusty winds 
will be the primary hazard across northeast Nebraska, with PoPs of 
50-75% in place, decreasing southward. 

Tuesday...

High temperatures on Tuesday will depend on how quick the northeast-
to-southwest oriented cold front pushes southward across the area. 
Highs are expected to reach the mid to upper 90s, with heat index 
values around 102-108, across southeast NE and southwest IA, 
with values peaking in the upper 80s further north where the 
front passes through before peak daytime heating. A Heat
Advisory will likely be needed for portions of the area, with 
the extent depending on timing of the front and cloud cover
extent. Scattered showers remain possible along and behind the 
front through the day. 

Another round of storms, with a few strong to severe, is expected 
Tuesday afternoon and evening across eastern Nebraska into southwest 
Iowa as the front pushes through a more unstable airmass. With the 
better large-scale forcing for ascent displaced to the northeast, 
details will likely hinge on mesoscale features that come into focus 
with time. Shear appears to be the limiting factor, though may 
be sufficient for a stronger cores that eventually push out 
pockets of hail and gusty winds. PoPs will taper off from north 
to south into early Wednesday.

Wednesday and Beyond...

Zonal flow aloft will return by mid-week, pushing high temperatures 
back into the 80s, with a few locations only peaking in the upper
70s on Wednesday and Thursday. Overnight lows into Thursday 
morning are expected to dip into the upper 50s and low 60s. For 
reference, Omaha last dipped below 60 degrees on August 27, with
the previous occurrence all the way back on June 23, so the 
morning should feel noticeably crisp. A brief mid-level ridge
sliding across the area will push Friday highs back into the
upper 80s.

Relatively dry conditions are expected through the remainder of the 
work week, though a weak shortwave bringing periodic precipitation 
chances can't be ruled out. Good news for the fall-lovers, looking 
further ahead, most GEFS and EPS-AIFS members bring a potent trough 
across the northern Plains next weekend. This system will bring a 
push of cooler air into the region and could knock highs in the 70s 
by the end of next weekend, though details on timing and extent will 
still need to be ironed out. The passage also brings PoPs of 30-40% 
back into the region.
